title: Upstream non-AUG initiation and ribosomal -1 frameshifting in ATXN8OS CTA/CTG repeat-associated translation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed all 37 files in the Mendeley deposit via its public API (total 4.07 GB) and downloaded and printed all 20 CSV files (39-737 bytes each, 2-8 data rows each, ~371 numeric values in total). Also read the open-access full text: data availability statement, methods, and figure/table mentions.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: What the numbers mean physically (luciferase reporter units, fold changes, frameshifting efficiency) comes from the figure legends, not from the files. I did not open the 17 TIFF images (14 western-blot scans ~3 MB each, three microscopy movie stacks of ~1.34 GB each). The Europe PMC supplementary-file endpoint timed out at 135 s, so Supplementary Tables S1-S3 (plasmid, oligonucleotide and antibody lists) were not retrieved; the main text says they are lists of reagents, not measurement tables.

a1_downloadable.note: Mendeley Data deposit is public under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; I downloaded all 20 CSV files with no login.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Each CSV column is a construct/condition and each cell is the measured reporter signal, so the outcome is a value in the file, already normalised by the authors in most files.

a3_inputs_present.note: No sequences anywhere in the files. The model input (the 5' leader plus CTA/CTG repeat sequence of each reporter) exists only as prose in Methods plus four Addgene plasmid identifiers, so every input would have to be reconstructed by hand.

a4_units_stated.note: Not one CSV has a units row or a header beyond the construct name. Fig.2C holds raw luminescence, Fig.2E ratios, Fig.4B fold changes; units are only inferable from figure legends and are inconsistent across files.

a5_enough_rows.note: Counted in the downloaded files: 20 CSVs, 2-8 rows each, ~371 numeric measurements spanning roughly 90 distinct construct-by-condition groups with 3-6 replicates. The checklist needs ~1,500 labelled rows (~400 for classification).

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~6 KB of CSV text; the whole deposit is 4.07 GB only because of three ~1.34 GB movie TIFFs that the proposed task does not need.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-feasible, but that is because there is almost no data.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Replicate counts in the CSVs (labelled lot1-lot6) match the 3 or 6 independent translation lots described in the figure legends; nothing disagrees.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are physical measurements: NanoLuc/firefly luciferase light output from in vitro translation lots and transfected cells, plus single-molecule imaging. No model-derived or feature-derived values.

existing_models.name: FScanpy (2026, Zoological Research) - semi-supervised hybrid framework for programmed ribosomal frameshifting sites
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.951; split details not checked (search abstract only).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Cross-species generalisation of frameshift determinants; they report AAA/GGG motifs and messenger RNA secondary-structure stability as the main drivers.

existing_models.name: PRFect (BMC Bioinformatics 2024) - machine-learning detector of programmed ribosomal frameshifts in prokaryotic and viral genomes
existing_models.score_and_split: Not checked; the paper is a tool paper with reported detection performance on curated prokaryotic/viral frameshift sites.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Eukaryotic and repeat-expansion frameshifting is outside its training scope.

existing_models.name: KnotInFrame (Nucleic Acids Research 2008) - RNA-folding-based -1 frameshift predictor
existing_models.score_and_split: Pre-deep-learning; evaluated on small curated frameshift site sets.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Distinguishing true -1 frameshift signals from random slippery-site-plus-structure matches.

existing_models.name: TIS Predictor (PLOS One 2021) - machine learning for translation initiation sites in nucleotide-repeat-expansion neurologic diseases
existing_models.score_and_split: Authors report beating the earlier deep model TITER by >18% in accuracy; split not checked.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Which non-AUG codon actually initiates in a given repeat-expansion transcript, the exact question this paper answers experimentally.

existing_models.name: TITER (Bioinformatics 2017) and MetaTIS (2025) - deep models for cognate and near-cognate translation initiation sites in human transcripts
existing_models.score_and_split: TITER is an ensemble of 32 neural networks scored on ribosome-profiling-derived initiation sites; MetaTIS combines genomic and protein language models on Ensembl annotations plus five initiation-site datasets.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Class imbalance and the weakness of near-cognate (non-AUG) initiation signals.

existing_models.name: Mikl et al., Nature Communications 2020 - high-throughput interrogation of programmed ribosomal frameshifting in human cells
existing_models.score_and_split: Not a predictor per se but a massively parallel reporter library; it is the data a sequence-to-frameshifting model would actually be trained on.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Sequence rules of frameshifting beyond the classic slippery site and pseudoknot.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer / DNABERT-2 / RNA-FM would be the natural RNA-sequence backbones
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would be ample for ~20 sequences, which is exactly the problem: far too few examples to fit any head.
backbone.licence: Backbone licences are permissive to non-commercial; the data is Creative Commons Attribution 4.0.

integration.partner_dataset: Mikl et al. 2020 massively parallel programmed-frameshifting reporter library in human cells, and ribosome-profiling initiation-site sets behind TITER/MetaTIS
integration.join_key: reporter insert nucleotide sequence (no shared standard identifier exists)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequence rules learned from large synthetic frameshifting libraries predict the frameshifting efficiency measured in disease repeat-expansion transcripts such as ATXN8OS? - but this paper contributes only ~90 condition groups to that question, so it is a validation anecdote, not a dataset.

controls.positive_control: The paper's own repeat-length dependence (0 vs 13 vs 80 repeats raises poly L signal ~1.0 to ~2.2 to ~7.1 fold in Fig.4B) is a known effect any model must recover.
controls.negative_control: The mutAUG&CUG construct collapses to ~0.04 of wild type in Fig.3F - a built-in near-zero condition.
controls.external_validation: None within this paper; would require the Mikl et al. 2020 library or published ATXN8/C9orf72 repeat-associated non-AUG translation reporter data.

honest_claim_h3: With 371 measurements over ~90 construct-by-condition groups from one laboratory and one reporter design, any model here could only claim to interpolate between the handful of ATXN8OS reporter variants this lab happened to build - not to predict non-AUG initiation or frameshifting for new sequences.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the messenger RNA sequence around a disease repeat to predict how often ribosomes start translation there and slip frames.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one reporter construct's leader-plus-repeat sequence. Verified count: about 90 distinct construct-by-condition groups, 371 individual measurements, across 20 small files.
plain_idea.predict: Two numbers per sequence: how much protein is made without a normal AUG start codon, and the fraction of ribosomes that shift back one nucleotide into a different reading frame. Both come from luciferase light-output assays in cell-free extracts and transfected cells, plus single-molecule microscopy.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs studying repeat-expansion diseases (spinocerebellar ataxia type 8, ALS, Huntington's) would like a sequence rule for which repeats make toxic hidden proteins; but this paper's data is far too small to fit one.

more_or_better_data.why: 371 measurements over ~90 groups, versus tens of thousands of designed reporters in the Mikl et al. 2020 human frameshifting library and genome-scale ribosome-profiling initiation sets used by TITER and MetaTIS.

confidence_score.why: There are 3-6 replicate lots per condition, so within-condition noise is estimable, but with ~90 groups there is no way to calibrate per-prediction confidence for unseen sequences.

models_beatable.why: KnotInFrame is from 2008 and PRFect targets prokaryotes/viruses, so they are dated for this task; but FScanpy (2026, reported area under the curve 0.951) and MetaTIS (2025, language-model based) are recent, and this dataset is far too small to challenge either.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the size condition outright: our data cannot even train a model, let alone see everything an existing model sees plus more, and the reporter assay here is not the same measurement the published models were fitted to.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: fit a sequence-to-function model (frozen RNA/DNA language-model embeddings plus a small regression head) mapping reporter leader-plus-repeat sequence to non-AUG initiation strength and -1 frameshifting efficiency, using this paper's reporter panel. Dead on arrival because the deposit contains only figure source data: ~90 condition groups, no sequences, no units.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed, from the actual byte sizes I downloaded: ~6 KB of CSV plus at most ~20 short sequences to embed. Compute is a non-issue; the dataset size is the issue.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the Mendeley deposit and count rows in its CSVs - 20 files of 2-8 rows, ~371 numbers in total. Five minutes, and it kills the project.

verdict_reason: Part A5 fails hard, and A3 and A4 with it. The deposited data is per-figure source data for a mechanism paper: 20 CSVs of 2-8 rows (~371 luciferase measurements over ~90 construct-by-condition groups), 14 western-blot TIFFs and three ~1.34 GB microscopy movie stacks. No construct sequences are in the files (they live in Methods prose and four Addgene plasmid identifiers), no units are stated in any CSV, and the DIA/SWATH mass-spectrometry proteome is not deposited anywhere (no ProteomeXchange, PRIDE or jPOST accession in the text). The underlying question - predicting non-AUG initiation and -1 frameshifting from sequence - is genuinely interesting and partly served by recent models (FScanpy 2026, MetaTIS 2025), but the data to pursue it is the Mikl et al. 2020 massively parallel reporter library, not this paper.
